title: Catalog API GET /v1/items pagination draft selection
purpose: Document two competing GET /v1/items response and pagination drafts and the unresolved selection so a human can choose a contract before implementation.

scope.text: This handoff covers the GET /v1/items response shape and pagination behavior described in two draft alternatives.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects Catalog API draft A, an API client can retrieve items from GET /v1/items using a JSON object response with an items array and a next_cursor string, and the UI can move to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected Catalog API draft A, when an API client calls GET /v1/items, then the response is a JSON object that contains an items array and a next_cursor string.
Given a human has selected Catalog API draft A, when the response contains a next_cursor string, then the UI provides a way to move to the next page using that next_cursor.

stories.text: If a human selects Catalog API draft B, an API client can retrieve items from GET /v1/items using a top-level JSON array and page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected Catalog API draft B, when an API client calls GET /v1/items, then the response is a top-level JSON array.
Given a human has selected Catalog API draft B, when an API client calls GET /v1/items with page and page_size query parameters, then those query parameters are used for pagination.

edge_cases.text: Draft A and draft B describe incompatible response shapes: an object with an items array and next_cursor string versus a top-level JSON array.
Draft A includes a UI next-page requirement; draft B does not mention UI next-page behavior.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.

risks.text: If draft A is selected, draft B's top-level JSON array and page and page_size pagination behavior would not be met.
If draft B is selected, draft A's JSON object response with next_cursor and the UI next-page requirement would not be met.

success_metrics.text: When a human selects draft A, the draft A response-shape and UI next-page acceptance criteria pass when exercised.
When a human selects draft B, the draft B response-shape and query-parameter pagination acceptance criteria pass when exercised.

open_questions: Which Catalog API draft (A or B) should a human select as authoritative?
Who has authority to select the draft?
